editorial:
New York City is packed with people trying to figure out love, and this comedy follows several of them at once. Alice breaks up with her boyfriend to learn who she is on her own, while her wild roommate Robin pushes her into the single life. Around them, Lucy searches for a husband with spreadsheets, Meg faces an unexpected pregnancy, Tom tends bar and avoids commitment, and David tries dating while still grieving. The vibe is breezy, funny, and a little messy, with lots of dating disasters and honest moments about growing up.

Rebel Wilson gets the biggest laughs, and Dakota Johnson keeps Alice easy to root for. The pacing moves quickly, though the large cast means some stories feel rushed. The humor lands best when it mixes party energy with real heart, but a few jokes are predictable. If you want a light, feel-good rom-com for a girls' night or cozy weekend, this is a solid pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Alice realizes being single is not just a waiting period before the right person arrives. After heartbreaks and false starts, she chooses independence and solo travel instead of chasing a relationship. Meg embraces motherhood, Lucy softens her rigid search for love, Robin stays proudly unattached, and David's unreadiness shows not every connection is meant to last. The ending reframes single life as a confident choice.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves ensemble rom-coms and messy dating stories.
